title: Plantar hallux-versus-metatarsal sensory loss did not improve transferred gait-speed prediction beyond insensate-site counts
abstract: In public NHANES1999–2000 adults aged50+(n1755), we fitted gait-speed models and tested them without target refitting in separately recruited NHANES2001–2002 adults(n1801). A hallux-minus-metatarsal insensitivity contrast did not improve prediction beyond total insensate sites and conventional covariates: weighted MSE gain was -0.000301(m/s)^2;500 source-target participant-refit bootstrap95% interval[-0.001031,0.000048]. Joint strata-PSU refit bootstrap interval was[-0.001007,-0.000016]. Linear and saturated-count baselines, diabetes exclusion and added knee strength also showed negative gains. Exploratory cross-sectional AI-authored analysis; not equivalence, a causal result or clinical validation.
